- transfer_complete: Active-high signal indicating the transfer is complete

    input [7:0] x_range_max,

    input [7:0] y_range_max,

    output reg [7:0] x_coord,
    output reg [7:0] y_coord

    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start_channel_0,
    input wire start_channel_1,

    output reg [7:0] data_out_0,
    output reg [7:0] data_out_1,
    output reg done_0,
    output reg done_1
);

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00;
            data_out_0 <= 8'b0;
            data_out_1 <= 8'b0;
            done_0 <= 1'b0;
            done_1 <= 1'b0;

                        state <= 2'b01; // start transferring channel 0
                        data_out_0 <= source_address_0; // simulate data transfer
                        done_0 <= 1'b0;
                    end else if (start_channel_1) begin
                        state <= 2'b10; // start transferring channel 1
                        data_out_1 <= source_address_1; // simulate data transfer
                        done_1 <= 1'b0;
                    end
                end
                2'b01: begin // transferring channel 0
                    done_0 <= 1'b1; // transfer done for channel 0
                    state <= 2'b00; // back to idle
                end
                2'b10: begin // transferring channel 1
                    done_1 <= 1'b1; // transfer done for channel 1
                    state <= 2'b00; // back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end

description: Create a simple SPI controller that transmits a byte of data when a start signal is received. The controller should shift out one bit of data on the SPI MOSI line on each rising edge of the SPI clock. The SPI clock should be generated internally.
code:
module spi_controller (
    input clk,       // System clock
    input start,     // Start transmission signal
    input [7:0] data_in, // 8-bit data input
    output reg mosi, // Master Out Slave In
    output reg sck,   // SPI clock output
    output reg done    // Transmission done signal
);
    reg [2:0] bit_cnt; // Bit counter
    reg [7:0] shift_reg; // Shift register for data
    reg state; // State variable

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (start) begin
            shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data
            bit_cnt <= 3'b000; // Reset counter
            sck <= 0; // Initialize clock
            done <= 0; // Reset done signal
            state <= 1; // Start the transmission
        end else if (state) begin
            sck <= ~sck; // Toggle clock
            if (sck) begin // On rising edge of SCK
                mosi <= shift_reg[7]; // Output the most significant bit
                shift_reg <= {shift_reg[6:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
                bit_cnt <= bit_cnt + 1; // Increment bit counter
                if (bit_cnt == 3'b111) begin
                    done <= 1; // Set done signal after 8 bits
                    state <= 0; // Stop the transmission
                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

module I2C_Controller (
    input wire clk,            // System clock
    input wire start,          // Start condition signal
    input wire [7:0] data,     // Data to be sent
    output reg SDA,            // Data line
    output reg busy            // Busy indicator
);

    reg [3:0] state;           // State machine state
    reg [2:0] bit_count;       // Bit counter

    // State encoding
    localparam IDLE      = 4'b0000,
               START     = 4'b0001,
               SEND_DATA = 4'b0010,
               STOP      = 4'b0011;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                busy <= 0;
                if (start) begin
                    state <= START;
                    busy <= 1;
                end
            end
            
            START: begin
                SDA <= 0; // Start condition
                state <= SEND_DATA;
            end
            
            SEND_DATA: begin
                if (bit_count < 8) begin
                    SDA <= data[7 - bit_count]; // Send MSB first
                    bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
                end else begin
                    state <= STOP;
                end
            end
            
            STOP: begin
                SDA <= 1; // Stop condition
                busy <= 0;
                state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle
                bit_count <= 0; // Reset bit count
            end
            
            default: state <= IDLE;
        endcase
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Kogge-Stone Adder in Verilog that takes two 5-bit binary numbers as inputs and produces a 6-bit output representing their sum. The adder should implement the Kogge-Stone prefix network to compute the carry bits and then use those carries to compute the sum bits.
code:
module KoggeStoneAdder (
    input [4:0] A,
    input [4:0] B,
    output [5:0] SUM
);
    wire [4:0] P; // Propagate
    wire [4:0] G; // Generate
    wire [4:0] C; // Carry

    assign P = A ^ B; // Propagate
    assign G = A & B; // Generate

    // Carry computation using Kogge-Stone
    assign C[0] = 0; // No carry-in
    assign C[1] = G[0]; // C1 = G0
    assign C[2] = G[1] | (P[1] & G[0]); // C2 = G1 + P1*G0
    assign C[3] = G[2] | (P[2] & G[1]) | (P[2] & P[1] & G[0]); // C3
    assign C[4] = G[3] | (P[3] & G[2]) | (P[3] & P[2] & G[1]) | (P[3] & P[2] & P[1] & G[0]); // C4

    // Sum computation
    assign SUM = {C[4], P[4] ^ C[4], P[3] ^ C[3], P[2] ^ C[2], P[1] ^ C[1], P[0] ^ C[0]};

endmodule

The I2C protocol requires proper timing for the SDA and SCL signals during data transmission.
code:
module i2c_master (
    input clk,
    input start,
    input stop,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg sda,
    output reg scl
);
    reg [3:0] state;
    reg [7:0] data_buffer;
    integer bit_index;

    parameter IDLE = 0;
    parameter START = 1;
    parameter TRANSFER = 2;
    parameter STOP = 3;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                sda <= 1;  // Idle state SDA high
                scl <= 1;  // Idle state SCL high
                if (start) begin
                    state <= START;
                end
            end

            START: begin
                sda <= 0;  // Start condition
                state <= TRANSFER;
                data_buffer <= data_in; // Load data for transfer
                bit_index <= 0;
            end

            TRANSFER: begin
                scl <= 0;  // Prepare to send
                sda <= data_buffer[7 - bit_index]; // Send MSB first
                bit_index <= bit_index + 1;
                if (bit_index == 7) begin
                    state <= STOP; // Move to stop after sending all bits
                end
            end

            STOP: begin
                scl <= 1;  // Stop condition
                sda <= 1;  // SDA goes high after SCL
                state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle
            end

            default: state <= IDLE;
        endcase
    end
endmodule
